To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mouse claustral projection neurons project to a wide range of cortical regions, but not subcortical ones, and receive inputs from a wide range of brain areas.
the mouse claustral output is widespread and uniform and the input is limbic and neuromodulating.
the mouse claustral principal neurons project to a variety of higher order cortical regions, and receive inputs from limbic structures and neuromodulators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the neural circuits of the brain, specifically the claustrums of the brain.
the organization and function of cortical‐claustral networks in mice.
the role of the CLA in cortical information processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mouse claustral neurons have a complex organization and are involved in the integration of information related to the salience of stimuli.

the mouse claustral system is a highly complex network with multiple functions, including a role in the processing of sensory‐related information, the integration of limbic and sensory information and the modulation of cortical state.
the claustrums' function remains unclear, although it has been implicated in a variety of processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CLA receives a diverse array of inputs from limbic regions, and projects its output to a wide range of cortical areas.
CLA is an output structure of the limbic system that broadcasts its information to a wide range of cortical regions, which is a novel function that has not previously been described.
CLA neurons receive widespread cortical and subcorticocortical input, and project broadly to cortical regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the claustrums is a highly integrative structure that receives input and projects to multiple brain regions.
the CLA is an important hub for integrating information across multiple sensory modalities and cognitive systems.
CLA neurons are not a homogeneous population, but rather are organized by their projection targets.
